'''''Zelkova carpinifolia''''', known as  '''Caucasian zelkova''', '''Caucasian elm'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> or just '''zelkova''', is a species of ''[[Zelkova]]'', native to the [[Caucasus]], [[Kaçkar Mountains|Kaçkar]], and [[Alborz]] mountains of eastern Europe and southwest Asia.

[[Image:Zelkova carpinifolia0.jpg|thumb|Fruit, late autumn]]
It is a medium-sized to large [[deciduous]] [[tree]] growing to {{convert|20|-|35|m|abbr=on}} tall, with a trunk of up to {{convert|2|m|abbr=on}}  in diameter. The crown is a highly distinctive vase-shape, with a short broad trunk dividing low down into numerous nearly erect branches. The [[leaf|leaves]] are alternate, {{convert|4|-|10|cm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|2.5|-|6|cm|abbr=on|frac=8}} broad, the margin bluntly serrated with 7–12 teeth on each side. The [[flower]]s are inconspicuous and greenish, with no petals, and are wind-pollinated. The [[fruit]] is a small [[nut (fruit)|nutlet]] {{convert|5|-|6|mm|abbr=on|frac=16}} in diameter.

It is grown as an [[ornamental tree]] in Europe (huge exemplars of it can be found quite often in the western [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] province of [[Imereti]], used for decorating courtyards in villages and providing pleasant shade) and more rarely in North America (where the related Japanese ''[[Zelkova serrata|Z. serrata]]'' is more popular).
;Hybrid cultivars
*[[Zelkova 'Verschaffeltii'|''Zelkova × verschaffeltii'']]

== Distribution ==
The two main population centres of ''Z. carpinifolia'' are in the [[Hyrcanian forest]] of southern Azerbaijan and northern Iran, and the [[Colchic Forest|Colchic forest]] of western Georgia. Other isolated stands can be found in the [[Karabakh mountain]]s, Anatolia, northwestern and eastern Georgia, and Iranian Kurdistan.<ref>Bétrisey, S., Yousefzadeh, H. & Kozlowski, G. 2018. ''Zelkova carpinifolia''. The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2018: e.T31303A131166773. {{doi|10.2305/IUCN.UK.2018-}}</ref>
